title: Chapter 12 — The Chair at the Back Side
description: After Professor: an empty chair, a notebook of rules, and a street that doesn't know yet who it listens to.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: A week after. The Back Side wakes up at 5 a.m. like it always does. The drivers shout. The danfos cough. Something is wrong and it takes you a minute to see what: the chair.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Professor's chair is empty. Somebody has put a tea glass on it, the way he liked it, too sweet. Nobody sits there. Even the drivers walk around it.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Professor's chair is empty. He is in Kirikiri, for your crime. Somebody has written on the wall above it in chalk: "RULE ONE: KNOW WHO YOU OWE."

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Professor's chair is empty. He is in the village with his sister and her goats. He sends a voice note every morning that is mostly goat.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Professor's chair is at his buka now, by the Front Stop. He sits on it to supervise the rice. Nobody has ever supervised rice so seriously.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Professor is in his chair. But he is slower, and he lets you answer the drivers before he does. You notice. He notices you noticing.

beats.speaker: professor
beats.text: Before the book. Sit. One game of draughts. I want to see if you learned anything except shouting.

won.toast: Professor stares at the board for a whole minute. Then he laughs, properly.

lost.toast: "Rule eleven," he says. "Never play an old man at his own table."

beats.speaker: garba
beats.text: He played every evening on this table. Bottle tops. Red for him, green for whoever was foolish. (He sets up the board.) Play me. For him.

won.toast: Garba nods slowly. "He taught you that move. I saw him do it to me in 2009."

lost.toast: Garba wins, and doesn't celebrate. He leaves the red bottle tops on Professor's chair.

beats.speaker: garba
beats.text: (handing you a school exercise book, its cover soft with age) Professor gave me this years ago. He said: "When I'm gone, give it to the one who argues with me most." (He shrugs.) That's you.

beats.speaker: professor
beats.text: (handing you a school exercise book, its cover soft with age) My rules. Forty years. Fifty-two rules, three crossed out, one in my son's handwriting. (He doesn't say anything else.) Keep it.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: RULE 1: Know who you owe. RULE 7: The rain doesn't care who you are. RULE 19: Never let a driver see you count. RULE 33: Your mother is always listening, even in Lagos.

beats.speaker: player
beats.text: The last page is empty except for the number 53.

options.text: Write your own rule 53, and start teaching it to the new JJCs at the Back Side.
Keep the book in your pocket. Read it when you need it.
"Rules are for old men." Leave it on the chair.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: A boy gets off the night bus with one bag and a face you recognise. You had it. Somebody is already walking towards him with a receipt book. The receipts are blank.

beats.speaker: player
beats.text: The boy is about to pay the "loading fee".

options.text: Step in. "Rule number one: in Lagos, nobody gives you a receipt for nothing." Show him the way to the Back Side.
Let Lagos teach him. It taught you.

beats.speaker: player
beats.text: The boy follows you around for a week, asking questions. Then three more boys come. Then a girl. They sit on crates around the empty chair and you talk until the drivers come.

options.text: This is the work. Let the park and the elections go. Teach.
Teach in the mornings. Collect in the afternoons. You can do both.

beats.speaker: mama
beats.text: (on the phone) {name}. I heard about your old teacher. (She is quiet.) Did you thank him? Before? (She doesn't wait for an answer.) You must thank people while they can hear.

variants.text: (on the phone) I heard about Professor. The one who stood up when I came. (She is quiet.) An agbero who stands up for an old woman. Your father would have liked him. Did you thank him?
(on the phone) I heard about your "transport" colleague. Professor. (A pause.) {name}, a man with three fingers doesn't work in an office in Ikeja. I am old. I am not blind. Not any more.

beats.speaker: mama
beats.text: And greet Ada. Tell her the fan was good. Tell her my son is slow, but he gets there.

beats.speaker: biodun
beats.text: (hooting from the road) Village boy! The key is still on a string! Any time!

beats.title: The Chair at the Back Side
beats.summary: An empty chair, a notebook of rules, and a new JJC at the bus stop. Election season is coming, and the street doesn't know yet whose voice it listens to now.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: You give your fee book to Scatter. You give your stick to nobody. Every morning at 5 a.m., on crates around Professor's chair, you teach the rules to whoever came on the night bus.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: The drivers bring tea. Garba refuses payment. Bassey, passing, stops to listen to Rule 19 and laughs out loud, once, and then pretends he didn't.

beats.title: The New Professor
beats.summary: You never sat in the chair. You sat beside it, and taught. The Back Side has a teacher again.
